title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
summary: RACE replaces full-dimensional per-head keys and queries (and reconstruction-based KV-cache compression) with a natively reduced-dimensional attention formed by selecting complete RoPE rotary pairs ranked by joint query-key activation energy, folding the selection into the model weights post-training. It costs a one-time calibration pass and permanently removes up to half of the head dimension, trading some representational capacity for lower KV-cache memory and attention FLOPs without custom kernels. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of production inputs, if accuracy on zero-shot or long-context tasks degrades at the chosen compression level, or if short-context workloads see little benefit since the gains concentrate at long contexts.
rationale: It is a post-training, kernel-free method compatible with a single-GPU budget and offers meaningful memory and throughput gains, but the 1.79x figure is measured at 256K context and quality retention depends on calibration, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: RoPE-aligned head-dimension KV-cache compression via rotary-pair selection

claims.statement: RACE replaces full-dimensional per-head keys and queries (and reconstruction-based KV-cache compression) with a natively reduced-dimensional attention formed by selecting complete RoPE rotary pairs ranked by joint query-key activation energy, folding the selection into the model weights post-training. It costs a one-time calibration pass and permanently removes up to half of the head dimension, trading some representational capacity for lower KV-cache memory and attention FLOPs without custom kernels. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of production inputs, if accuracy on zero-shot or long-context tasks degrades at the chosen compression level, or if short-context workloads see little benefit since the gains concentrate at long contexts.

At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower TTFT, and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory versus the uncompressed model.
